Nobody with that email is an answer too (found is false), not a failure. monthly_amount is what they pay per month as a number, to compare with an amount such as 1000.

parameters.description: The customer's email address, such as the address a support ticket came from. An address that finds nobody as typed is tried again in lower case. Needed unless you choose a customer.

found.description: True when Stripe has a customer with this email (or id). When false, summary says nobody was found, the two statuses are none and the rest is blank.

has_active_subscription.description: True when their subscription is active or on a free trial.

last_payment_amount.description: Beta. The amount of that payment as a plain number in the currency's main unit, such as 49.0 for $49.00, to compare with a number; 0 when there is none.

last_payment_amount_display.description: The amount of that payment as a person writes it, such as $49.00; blank when there is none.

last_payment_date.description: The day that payment was started, as a date other steps can read, such as 2026-11-03 (UTC); blank when there is none.

last_payment_date_display.description: The same day as a person writes it, such as Nov 3, 2026.

last_payment_failed.description: True when their most recent payment failed. Use it in a condition, such as to raise a ticket's priority.

last_payment_failure_reason.description: Why the payment failed, in Stripe's words, such as Your card was declined; blank unless it failed.

last_payment_status.description: How their most recent payment went, one of: paid, failed (the card or bank refused it), pending (still going through, or waiting for the customer to confirm with their bank) or none (they have never been charged). It covers subscription renewals and one-off payments; a payment that was started and never tried doesn't count.

monthly_amount.description: Beta. What the customer pays per month, as a plain number in the currency's main unit, such as 1200.0 for $1,200.00: their active subscriptions added up, quantities included, with a yearly price divided by 12 and a weekly one multiplied by 52 and divided by 12. Before discounts and tax. 0 when they have no active subscription. Compare it with a number, such as monthly_amount greater than 1000, to pick out customers who pay more than $1,000 a month.

monthly_amount_display.description: Beta. The same monthly amount as a person writes it, such as $1,200.00, for a message; blank when they have no active subscription.

name.description: The customer's name; blank when Stripe has none.

plan_name.description: The plan they are on now: the name of the product they subscribe to, such as Pro. Several are separated by commas. Blank when they have no current subscription.

subscription_status.description: Where their subscription stands, one of: active, trialing (on a free trial), past_due (a renewal payment failed and Stripe is still trying), unpaid, paused, incomplete (the first payment hasn't gone through), canceled (they had one and it ended) or none (they never had one).

summary.description: The plan and the last payment in one short paragraph, ready to paste into a note or message: 'Plan: Pro (active). Last payment: $49.00 on Nov 3, 2026, paid.' When nobody is found: 'No Stripe customer with this email.'

output.event_id: The id of the Stripe event (evt_...).

output.evidence_due_date: Beta. The last day your evidence can reach Stripe, as a date other steps can read, such as 2026-11-30 (UTC). Give it to a step that sets a due date or counts days from a date; blank when Stripe set no deadline.
output.evidence_due_display: Beta. That deadline as a person writes it, such as Nov 30, 2026. Use it in a message.
output.metadata: Your own key-value data saved on the dispute.
output.payer: Beta. Who disputed, ready to put in a message: their name, else their email, else 'a customer'.
output.previous_attributes: What it was before, for the parts that changed only, such as status or items.
output.previous_status: Beta. The status before this change, such as trialing, when the status changed; blank when it didn't. Compare it with status to catch a trial becoming paid or a subscription falling past_due.
output.reason: Why the customer's bank says it's disputed, as Stripe's code, such as fraudulent or product_not_received. For a message use reason_display.
output.reason_display: Beta. Why it's disputed, in words, such as Product not received, Fraudulent or Charged twice. Use it in a message.
output.status: Where it stands, such as needs_response or warning_needs_response.

stripe_subscription_updated_trigger.description: Beta. Runs whenever a subscription changes in Stripe: a new plan or quantity, a trial becoming paid, a renewal, a payment falling past due, or a cancellation booked for the end of the period. Says what it was before.

output.amount_display: Beta. What it bills each period, such as $29.00 a month.
output.cancel_at_period_end: Whether it is set to end when the period it is in ends.
output.canceled_at: When it was canceled, as a Unix timestamp, if it was.

output.change_type: Beta. Which way the plan moved, in these words: upgrade (it now costs more a month), downgrade (less), plan change (a different plan at the same monthly amount) or no plan change (a renewal, a status change or anything else that left the plan and quantity alone).

output.metadata: Your own key-value data saved on the subscription.

stripe_trial_ending_trigger.description: Beta. Runs three days before a subscription's free trial ends in Stripe, or straight away for a trial shorter than three days. Says who the customer is, the day the trial ends and whether they have added a payment method.

output.amount_display: Beta. What it will bill each period once the trial ends, such as $29.00 a month.
output.cancel_at_period_end: Whether it is set to end when the trial does, instead of becoming paid.
output.created: When the subscription was created, as a Unix timestamp.
output.customer_email: The customer's email address, blank when Stripe has none.
output.customer_name: The customer's name, blank when Stripe has none.
output.customer_url: Beta. A link that opens the customer in the Stripe dashboard.
output.event_created: When the event happened, as a Unix timestamp.
output.event_id: The id of the Stripe event (evt_...).
output.has_payment_method: Beta. True when Stripe has a card or other payment method to charge when the trial ends: one saved on the subscription, or the customer's default. False when they haven't added one, or when Stripe wouldn't let the customer be read.
output.items: What is subscribed to: each item's price, product and quantity.
output.metadata: Your own key-value data saved on the subscription.
output.payer: Who the customer is, ready to put in a message: their name, else their email, else 'a customer'.
output.plan: Beta. The plan's name, when its price has one.
output.trial_end: Beta. When the trial ends, as a date and time other steps can read, such as 2026-11-30T09:00:00Z (UTC). For an email or message use trial_end_display.
output.trial_end_display: Beta. The day the trial ends as a person writes it, such as Nov 30, 2026, ready for an email or message with no date step.
output.what_happens_next: Beta. One or two sentences written to the customer saying what the end of the trial brings for them, ready to put in a reminder email as it is: that they will be charged the payment method they saved, that their subscription ends, pauses or cannot start unless they add one (by how the Stripe account treats a trial with no payment method), or that it ends with the trial because they cancelled. With it a reminder needs no decision of its own.
